VFS CACHING

This section describes the VFS cache settings.

VFS CACHING OVERVIEW

The VFS layer caches files on the local disk to improve performance. It can be used to implement the cache for operations on remotes.

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

If using --vfs-cache-max-size or --vfs-cache-min-free-space note that the cache may exceed these quotas for two reasons. Firstly because it is only checked every --vfs-cache-poll-interval. Secondly because open files cannot be evicted from the cache. When --vfs-cache-max-size or --vfs-cache-min-free-space is exceeded, rclone will attempt to evict the least accessed files from the cache first. rclone will start with files that haven't been accessed for the longest. This cache flushing strategy is efficient and more relevant files are likely to remain cached.

The --vfs-cache-max-age will evict files from the cache after the set time since last access has passed. The default value of 1 hour will start evicting files from cache that haven't been accessed for 1 hour. When a cached file is accessed the 1 hour timer is reset to 0 and will wait for 1 more hour before evicting. Specify the time with standard notation, s, m, h, d, w .

You should not run two copies of rclone using the same VFS cache with the same or overlapping remotes if using --vfs-cache-mode > off. This can potentially cause data corruption if you do. You can work around this by giving each rclone its own cache hierarchy with --cache-dir. You don't need to worry about this if the remotes in use don't overlap.

--vfs-cache-mode off

In this mode (the default) the cache will read directly from the remote and write directly to the remote without caching anything on disk.

This will mean some operations are not possible

•
Files can't be opened for both read AND write
•
Files opened for write can't be seeked
•
Existing files opened for write must have O_TRUNC set
•
Files open for read with O_TRUNC will be opened write only
•
Files open for write only will behave as if O_TRUNC was supplied
•
Open modes O_APPEND, O_TRUNC are ignored
•
If an upload fails it can't be retried

--vfs-cache-mode minimal

This is very similar to "off" except that files opened for read AND write will be buffered to disk. This means that files opened for write will be a lot more compatible, but uses the minimal disk space.

These operations are not possible

•
Files opened for write only can't be seeked
•
Existing files opened for write must have O_TRUNC set
•
Files opened for write only will ignore O_APPEND, O_TRUNC
•
If an upload fails it can't be retried

--vfs-cache-mode writes

In this mode files opened for read only are still read directly from the remote, write only and read/write files are buffered to disk first.

This mode should support all normal file system operations.

If an upload fails it will be retried at exponentially increasing intervals up to 1 minute.

--vfs-cache-mode full

In this mode all reads and writes are buffered to and from disk. When data is read from the remote this is buffered to disk as well.

In this mode the files in the cache will be sparse files and rclone will keep track of which bits of the files it has downloaded.

So if an application only reads the starts of each file, then rclone will only buffer the start of the file. These files will appear to be their full size in the cache, but they will be sparse files with only the data that has been downloaded present in them.

This mode should support all normal file system operations and is otherwise identical to --vfs-cache-mode writes.

When reading a file rclone will read --buffer-size plus --vfs-read-ahead bytes ahead. The --buffer-size is buffered in memory whereas the --vfs-read-ahead is buffered on disk.

When using this mode it is recommended that --buffer-size is not set too large and --vfs-read-ahead is set large if required.

IMPORTANT not all file systems support sparse files. In particular FAT/exFAT do not. Rclone will perform very badly if the cache directory is on a filesystem which doesn't support sparse files and it will log an ERROR message if one is detected.

Fingerprinting

Various parts of the VFS use fingerprinting to see if a local file copy has changed relative to a remote file. Fingerprints are made from:

•
size
•
modification time
•
hash

where available on an object.

On some backends some of these attributes are slow to read (they take an extra API call per object, or extra work per object).

For example hash is slow with the local and sftp backends as they have to read the entire file and hash it, and modtime is slow with the s3, swift, ftp and qinqstor backends because they need to do an extra API call to fetch it.

If you use the --vfs-fast-fingerprint flag then rclone will not include the slow operations in the fingerprint. This makes the fingerprinting less accurate but much faster and will improve the opening time of cached files.

If you are running a vfs cache over local, s3 or swift backends then using this flag is recommended.

Note that if you change the value of this flag, the fingerprints of the files in the cache may be invalidated and the files will need to be downloaded again.

VFS Chunked Reading

When rclone reads files from a remote it reads them in chunks. This means that rather than requesting the whole file rclone reads the chunk specified. This can reduce the used download quota for some remotes by requesting only chunks from the remote that are actually read, at the cost of an increased number of requests.

These flags control the chunking:

    --vfs-read-chunk-size SizeSuffix        Read the source objects in chunks (default 128M)
    --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit SizeSuffix  Max chunk doubling size (default off)
    --vfs-read-chunk-streams int            The number of parallel streams to read at once

The chunking behaves differently depending on the --vfs-read-chunk-streams parameter.

--vfs-read-chunk-streams == 0

Rclone will start reading a chunk of size --vfs-read-chunk-size, and then double the size for each read. When --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit is specified, and greater than --vfs-read-chunk-size, the chunk size for each open file will get doubled only until the specified value is reached. If the value is "off", which is the default, the limit is disabled and the chunk size will grow indefinitely.

With --vfs-read-chunk-size 100M and --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit 0 the following parts will be downloaded: 0-100M, 100M-200M, 200M-300M, 300M-400M and so on. When --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit 500M is specified, the result would be 0-100M, 100M-300M, 300M-700M, 700M-1200M, 1200M-1700M and so on.

Setting --vfs-read-chunk-size to 0 or "off" disables chunked reading.

The chunks will not be buffered in memory.

--vfs-read-chunk-streams > 0

Rclone reads --vfs-read-chunk-streams chunks of size --vfs-read-chunk-size concurrently. The size for each read will stay constant.

This improves performance performance massively on high latency links or very high bandwidth links to high performance object stores.

Some experimentation will be needed to find the optimum values of --vfs-read-chunk-size and --vfs-read-chunk-streams as these will depend on the backend in use and the latency to the backend.

For high performance object stores (eg AWS S3) a reasonable place to start might be --vfs-read-chunk-streams 16 and --vfs-read-chunk-size 4M. In testing with AWS S3 the performance scaled roughly as the --vfs-read-chunk-streams setting.

Similar settings should work for high latency links, but depending on the latency they may need more --vfs-read-chunk-streams in order to get the throughput.

VFS Performance

These flags may be used to enable/disable features of the VFS for performance or other reasons. See also the chunked reading feature.

In particular S3 and Swift benefit hugely from the --no-modtime flag (or use --use-server-modtime for a slightly different effect) as each read of the modification time takes a transaction.

    --no-checksum     Don't compare checksums on up/download.
    --no-modtime      Don't read/write the modification time (can speed things up).
    --no-seek         Don't allow seeking in files.
    --read-only       Only allow read-only access.

Sometimes rclone is delivered reads or writes out of order. Rather than seeking rclone will wait a short time for the in sequence read or write to come in. These flags only come into effect when not using an on disk cache file.

    --vfs-read-wait duration   Time to wait for in-sequence read before seeking (default 20ms)
    --vfs-write-wait duration  Time to wait for in-sequence write before giving error (default 1s)

When using VFS write caching (--vfs-cache-mode with value writes or full), the global flag --transfers can be set to adjust the number of parallel uploads of modified files from the cache (the related global flag --checkers has no effect on the VFS).

    --transfers int  Number of file transfers to run in parallel (default 4)

Symlinks

By default the VFS does not support symlinks. However this may be enabled with ei

من الخيارات التالية:

    --links      ترجمة الروابط الرمزية من وإلى الملفات العادية بامتداد '.rclonelink'.
    --vfs-links  ترجمة الروابط الرمزية من وإلى الملفات العادية بامتداد '.rclonelink' لطبقة VFS

نظرًا لأن معظم أنظمة التخزين السحابية لا تدعم الروابط الرمزية مباشرة، يقوم rclone بتخزين الرابط الرمزي كملف عادي بامتداد خاص. لذا فإن ملفًا يظهر كرابط رمزي link-to-file.txt سيتم تخزينه على التخزين السحابي كـ link-to-file.txt.rclonelink وسيكون المحتوى هو المسار إلى وجهة الرابط الرمزي.

لاحظ أن --links يمكّن ترجمة الروابط الرمزية عالميًا في rclone - وهذا يشمل أي واجهة خلفية تدعم المفهوم (على سبيل المثال، الواجهة الخلفية المحلية). --vfs-links يمكّنه فقط لطبقة VFS.

هذا المخطط متوافق مع المخطط المستخدم بواسطة الواجهة الخلفية المحلية مع علامة --local-links (https://rclone.org/local/#symlinks-junction-points).

تم تصميم علامة --vfs-links لـ rclone mount و rclone nfsmount و rclone serve nfs.

لم يتم اختبارها مع أوامر rclone serve الأخرى حتى الآن.

أحد قيود التنفيذ الحالي هو أنه يتوقع من المستدعي حل الروابط الرمزية الفرعية. على سبيل المثال، بالنظر إلى شجرة الدليل هذه

.
├── dir
│   └── file.txt
└── linked-dir -> dir

ستقوم VFS بحل linked-dir بشكل صحيح ولكن ليس linked-dir/file.txt. هذه ليست مشكلة للأوامر التي تم اختبارها ولكنها قد تكون لمشكلات أخرى.

لاحظ أن هناك مشكلة معلقة مع دعم الروابط الرمزية، المشكلة #8245 (https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/8245) مع إنشاء ملفات مكررة عند نقل الروابط الرمزية إلى أدلة تحتوي على ملف بنفس الاسم (أو العكس).

حساسية حالة الأحرف في VFS

أنظمة الملفات في Linux حساسة لحالة الأحرف: يمكن أن يختلف ملفان فقط بحالة الأحرف، ويجب استخدام حالة الأحرف الدقيقة عند فتح ملف.

أنظمة الملفات في Windows الحديثة غير حساسة لحالة الأحرف ولكنها تحافظ عليها: على الرغم من أنه يمكن فتح الملفات الموجودة باستخدام أي حالة أحرف، إلا أن حالة الأحرف الدقيقة المستخدمة لإنشاء الملف يتم الحفاظ عليها وتوفرها للبرامج للاستعلام عنها. غير مسموح لملفين في نفس الدليل بالاختلاف فقط بحالة الأحرف.

عادةً ما تكون أنظمة الملفات على macOS غير حساسة لحالة الأحرف. من الممكن جعل أنظمة الملفات في macOS حساسة لحالة الأحرف ولكن هذا ليس الافتراضي.

تتحكم علامة VFS --vfs-case-insensitive في كيفية تعامل rclone مع هاتين الحالتين. إذا كانت قيمتها "false"، فإن rclone يمرر أسماء الملفات إلى الواجهة البعيدة كما هي. إذا كانت العلامة "true" (أو تظهر بدون قيمة على سطر الأوامر)، فقد يقوم rclone بإجراء "إصلاح" كما هو موضح أدناه.

قد يحدد المستخدم اسم ملف لفتحه / حذفه / إعادة تسميته / إلخ بحالة أحرف مختلفة عما هو مخزن على الواجهة البعيدة. إذا كان الوسيط يشير إلى ملف موجود بنفس الاسم بالضبط، فسيتم استخدام حالة الملف الموجود على القرص. ومع ذلك، إذا لم يتم العثور على اسم ملف بنفس الاسم بالضبط ولكن يوجد اسم يختلف فقط بحالة الأحرف، فسيقوم rclone بإصلاح الاسم بشفافية. يحدث هذا الإصلاح فقط عند طلب ملف موجود. يتم التحكم في حساسية حالة الأحرف لأسماء الملفات التي ينشئها rclone بواسطة الواجهة البعيدة الأساسية.

لاحظ أن حساسية حالة الأحرف لنظام التشغيل الذي يقوم بتشغيل rclone (الهدف) قد تختلف عن حساسية حالة الأحرف لنظام ملفات تقدمه rclone (المصدر). تتحكم العلامة فيما إذا كان سيتم إجراء "إصلاح" لتلبية الهدف.

إذا لم يتم توفير العلامة على سطر الأوامر، فإن قيمتها الافتراضية تعتمد على نظام التشغيل الذي يعمل عليه rclone: "true" على Windows و macOS، و "false" في حالات أخرى. إذا تم توفير العلامة بدون قيمة، فهي "true".

تتحكم علامة --no-unicode-normalization فيما إذا كان سيتم إجراء "إصلاح" مماثل لأسماء الملفات التي تختلف ولكنها مكافئة بشكل قياسي (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicode_equivalence) فيما يتعلق بـ unicode. يمكن أن يكون تطبيع Unicode مفيدًا بشكل خاص لمستخدمي macOS، الذين يفضلون شكل NFD بدلاً من NFC الذي تستخدمه معظم الأنظمة الأساسية الأخرى. لذلك يوصى بشدة بالاحتفاظ بالإعداد الافتراضي وهو false على macOS، لتجنب مشكلات توافق الترميز.

في حالة (من غير المحتمل على الأرجح) وجود أسماء ملفات مكررة متعددة في دليل بعد تطبيق تطبيع الحالة والأحرف، تسمح علامة --vfs-block-norm-dupes بإخفاء هذه التكرارات. يأتي هذا مع مفاضلة أداء، حيث سيحتاج rclone إلى مسح الدليل بأكمله بحثًا عن التكرارات عند سرد دليل. لهذا السبب، يوصى بترك هذا معطلاً إذا لم يكن مطلوبًا. ومع ذلك، قد يرغب مستخدمو macOS في التفكير في استخدامه، وإلا، إذا كان دليل الواجهة البعيدة يحتوي على إصدارات NFC و NFD لنفس اسم الملف، فسيحدث موقف غريب: سيظهر كلا الإصدارين من الملف في التركيب، وسيظهر كلاهما قابلين للتعديل، ومع ذلك، فإن تعديل أي إصدار سيؤدي فعليًا إلى تعديل إصدار NFD فقط في الخلفية. --vfs-block- norm-dupes يمنع هذا الارتباك عن طريق اكتشاف هذا السيناريو، وإخفاء التكرارات، وتسجيل خطأ، على غرار كيفية التعامل مع ذلك في rclone sync.

خيارات قرص VFS

تسمح لك هذه العلامة بتعيين إحصائيات نظام الملفات يدويًا. قد يكون مفيدًا عندما لا يمكن قراءة هذه الإحصائيات بشكل صحيح تلقائيًا.

    --vfs-disk-space-total-size    قم بتعيين حجم مساحة القرص الإجمالي يدويًا (مثال: 256G، افتراضي: -1)

تقرير بديل للبايتات المستخدمة

بعض الواجهات الخلفية، وأبرزها S3، لا تبلغ عن كمية البايتات المستخدمة. إذا كنت بحاجة إلى توفر هذه المعلومات عند تشغيل df على نظام الملفات، فقم بتمرير العلامة --vfs-used-is-size إلى rclone. مع ضبط هذه العلامة، بدلاً من الاعتماد على الواجهة الخلفية للإبلاغ عن هذه المعلومات، سيقوم rclone بمسح الواجهة البعيدة بأكملها بشكل مشابه لـ rclone size وحساب إجمالي المساحة المستخدمة بنفسه.

تحذير: على عكس rclone size، تتجاهل هذه العلامة المرشحات بحيث تكون النتيجة دقيقة. ومع ذلك، هذا غير فعال للغاية وقد يكلف الكثير من استدعاءات API مما يؤدي إلى رسوم إضافية. استخدمه كحل أخير وفقط مع التخزين المؤقت.

بيانات تعريف VFS

إذا استخدمت علامة --vfs-metadata-extension، فيمكنك جعل VFS تعرض الملفات التي تحتوي على البيانات الوصفية (https://rclone.org/docs/#metadata) كـ JSON blob. لن تظهر هذه الملفات في قائمة الدليل، ولكن يمكن الوصول إليها وفتحها وبمجرد فتحها ستظهر في قوائم الدليل حتى تنتهي صلاحية ذاكرة التخزين المؤقت للدليل.

لاحظ أن بعض الواجهات الخلفية لن تنشئ بيانات وصفية إلا إذا قمت بتمرير علامة --metadata.

على سبيل المثال، باستخدام rclone mount مع --metadata --vfs-metadata-extension .metadata نحصل على

$ ls -l /mnt/
total 1048577
-rw-rw-r-- 1 user user 1073741824 Mar  3 16:03 1G
$ cat /mnt/1G.metadata
{
        "atime": "2025-03-04T17:34:22.317069787Z",
        "btime": "2025-03-03T16:03:37.708253808Z",
        "gid": "1000",
        "mode": "100664",
        "mtime": "2025-03-03T16:03:39.640238323Z",
        "uid": "1000"
}
$ ls -l /mnt/
total 1048578
-rw-rw-r-- 1 user user 1073741824 Mar  3 16:03 1G
-rw-rw-r-- 1 user user        185 Mar  3 16:03 1G.metadata

إذا لم يكن للملف بيانات وصفية، فسيتم إرجاعها كـ {} وإذا كان هناك خطأ في قراءة البيانات الوصفية، فسيتم إرجاع الخطأ كـ {"error":"error string"}.

rclone serve dlna remote:path [flags]

خيارات

      --addr string                            عنوان IP:المنفذ أو :المنفذ لربط خادم DLNA HTTP به (الافتراضي ":7879")
      --announce-interval Duration             الفاصل الزمني بين إعلانات SSDP (الافتراضي 12m0s)
      --dir-cache-time Duration                الوقت لتخزين إدخالات الدليل مؤقتًا (الافتراضي 5m0s)
      --dir-perms FileMode                     أذونات الدليل (الافتراضي 777)
      --file-perms FileMode                    أذونات الملف (الافتراضي 666)
      --gid uint32                             تجاوز حقل gid الذي تم تعيينه بواسطة نظام الملفات (غير مدعوم على Windows) (الافتراضي 1000)
  -h, --help                                   المساعدة لـ dlna
      --interface stringArray                  الواجهة المراد استخدامها لـ SSDP (كرر حسب الحاجة)
      --link-perms FileMode                    أذونات الرابط (الافتراضي 666)
      --log-trace                              تمكين تسجيل تتبع حركة مرور SOAP
      --name string                            اسم خادم DLNA
      --no-checksum                            لا تقارن المجموع الاختباري عند التحميل / التنزيل
      --no-modtime                             لا تقرأ / تكتب وقت التعديل (يمكن أن يسرع الأمور)
      --no-seek                                لا تسمح بالبحث في الملفات
      --poll-interval Duration                 الوقت للانتظار بين استطلاع التغييرات، يجب أن يكون أصغر من dir-cache-time وفقط على الواجهات المدعومة (اضبط 0 لتعطيله) (الافتراضي 1m0s)
      --read-only                              السماح بالوصول للقراءة فقط
      --uid uint32                             تجاوز حقل uid الذي تم تعيينه بواسطة نظام الملفات (غير مدعوم على Windows) (الافتراضي 1000)
      --umask FileMode                         تجاوز بتات الإذن التي تم تعيينها بواسطة نظام الملفات (غير مدعوم على Windows) (الافتراضي 002)
      --vfs-block-norm-dupes                   إذا كانت هناك أسماء ملفات مكررة في نفس الدليل (بعد التطبيع)، سجل خطأ وأخفِ التكرارات (قد يكون له تكلفة أداء)
      --vfs-cache-max-age Duration             الحد الأقصى للوقت منذ آخر وصول للعناصر في ذاكرة التخزين المؤقت (الافتراضي 1h0m0s)
      --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix          الحد الأقصى للحجم الإجمالي للعناصر في ذاكرة التخزين المؤقت (الافتراضي معطل)
      --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix    الحد الأدنى للمساحة الحرة المستهدفة على القرص الذي يحتوي على ذاكرة التخزين المؤقت (الافتراضي معطل)
      --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode               وضع ذاكرة التخزين المؤقت off|minimal|writes|full (الافتراضي off)
      --vfs-cache-poll-interval Duration       الفاصل الزمني لاستطلاع ذاكرة التخزين المؤقت للعناصر القديمة (الافتراضي 1m0s)
      --vfs-case-insensitive                   إذا لم يتم العثور على اسم ملف، فابحث عن تطابق غير حساس لحالة الأحرف
      --vfs-disk-space-total-size SizeSuffix   حدد المساحة الإجمالية للقرص (الافتراضي معطل)
      --vfs-fast-fingerprint                   استخدم بصمات أصابع سريعة (أقل دقة) للكشف عن التغيير
      --vfs-links                              ترجمة الروابط الرمزية من وإلى الملفات العادية بامتداد '.rclonelink' لطبقة VFS
      --vfs-metadata-extension string          تعيين الامتداد لقراءة البيانات الوصفية

rclone serve restic

Serve any remote on the restic server protocol.

Synopsis

This command implements the Restic server protocol, allowing restic to use rclone as a data storage mechanism for various cloud providers.

To create a restic server, one must create a Unix or TCP socket that Restic will look for when you use the server, and then it listens for commands from the restic client and runs the corresponding code when necessary. Restic servers can run as a managed server under control of the restic daemon or as an independent native service. For testing, you can just run it directly from the command line, for example:

sudo rclone serve restic --socket-addr :8080 -vv

Running rclone serve restic will create the said socket, listening for commands from Restic to create the necessary repositories. Normally you need not give the --socket-addr flag. The API will listen on the unix domain socket at /run/restic/restic.sock. In the example above rclone will create a TCP socket and a small file /etc/restic/restic.spec containing the socket address. We use sudo because both paths are writeable only by the root user.

If you later decide to change listening socket, the restic daemon must be restarted to reconnect to /run/restic/restic.sock or parse new /etc/restic/restic.spec. Until you restart, any repository related restic commands will timeout trying to access the old socket. Running directly is supported on Linux only, not on Windows or MacOS. This is not a problem with managed server mode described in details in the full documentation (https://rclone.org/restic).

The command will create repository data under the path given by --data-dir (by default /var/lib/restic/restic available only to root) and maintain the JSON formatted file restic-server.state in the rclone cache directory with book-keeping records of created and mounted repositories.

All mount and VFS options are submitted by the restic daemon via API, but you can also provide defaults on the command line as well as set path to the config file and cache directory or adjust logging verbosity.

VFS - Virtual File System

This command uses the VFS layer. This adapts the cloud storage objects that rclone uses into something which looks much more like a disk filing system.

Cloud storage objects have lots of properties which aren't like disk files - you can't extend them or write to the middle of them, so the VFS layer has to deal with that. Because there is no one right way of doing this there are various options explained below.

The VFS layer also implements a directory cache - this caches info about files and directories (but not the data) in memory.

VFS Directory Cache

Using the --dir-cache-time flag, you can control how long a directory should be considered up to date and not refreshed from the backend. Changes made through the VFS will appear immediately or invalidate the cache.

    --dir-cache-time duration   Time to cache directory entries for (default 5m0s)
    --poll-interval duration    Time to wait between polling for changes. Must be smaller than dir-cache-time. Only on supported remotes. Set to 0 to disable (default 1m0s)

However, changes made directly on the cloud storage by the web interface or a different copy of rclone will only be picked up once the directory cache expires if the backend configured does not support polling for changes. If the backend supports polling, changes will be picked up within the polling interval.

You can send a SIGHUP signal to rclone for it to flush all directory caches, regardless of how old they are. Assuming only one rclone instance is running, you can reset the cache like this:

kill -SIGHUP $(pidof rclone)

If you configure rclone with a remote control then you can use rclone rc to flush the whole directory cache:

rclone rc vfs/forget

Or individual files or directories:

rclone rc vfs/forget file=path/to/file dir=path/to/dir

VFS File Buffering

The --buffer-size flag determines the amount of memory, that will be used to buffer data in advance.

Each open file will try to keep the specified amount of data in memory at all times. The buffered data is bound to one open file and won't be shared.

This flag is a upper limit for the used memory per open file. The buffer will only use memory for data that is downloaded but not not yet read. If the buffer is empty, only a small amount of memory will be used.

The maximum memory used by rclone for buffering can be up to --buffer-size * open files.

VFS File Caching

These flags control the VFS file caching options. File caching is necessary to make the VFS layer appear compatible with a normal file system. It can be disabled at the cost of some compatibility.

For example you'll need to enable VFS caching if you want to read and write simultaneously to a file. See below for more details.

Note that the VFS cache is separate from the cache backend and you may find that you need one or the other or both.

    --cache-dir string                     Directory rclone will use for caching.
    --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode             Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
    --vfs-cache-max-age duration           Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
    --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix        Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

Supported cache modes are:

•
off: No caching is done. All operations are done directly on the remote. This is the default mode.
•
minimal: Only cache files for reading. Write operations will be done directly on the remote. This mode is useful if you want to read files quickly without writing them. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that read files.
•
writes: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that write a lot of small files or that write frequently to files. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that write files.
•
full: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that need to read and write files frequently, and that require high performance. This mode has the highest compatibility with applications that read and write files.

VFS Options

These flags control the VFS layer behavior. They are used to tune the performance and compatibility of the VFS layer.

      --buffer-size SizeSuffix         Chunk size to buffer file data in RAM (default 16Mi)
      --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode       Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
      --vfs-cache-max-age duration     Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
      --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix  Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
      --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
      --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-disk-cache-recursive        If set, rclone will traverse directories recursively to find files for the disk cache
      --vfs-fast-fingerprint bool       If set, rclone will use a fast fingerprint for checking if files are already in the cache (default true)
      --vfs-fingerprint-method FingerprintHashMethod  Hash method to use for fingerprinting files for the cache (default --vfs-fast-fingerprint)
      --vfs-flag FileFlags               Set flags on VFS objects
      --vfs-flag-exclude stringArray     Exclude VFS objects from flags
      --vfs-flag-exclude-from stringArray  Read VFS flag exclude patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --vfs-flag-include stringArray     Include VFS objects in flags
      --vfs-flag-include-from stringArray  Read VFS flag include patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --vfs-get-content bool             Get the content of files when listing directories (default true)
      --vfs-get-pmod bool                Get the permissions of files when listing directories (default true)
      --vfs-implicit-dirs bool           Create implicit directories when writing files (default true)
      --vfs-lazy-get-pmod                Lazily get the permissions of files when listing directories
      --vfs-lazy-read                  If set, rclone will not read the content of files until they are opened
      --vfs-lock-timeout duration        Time to wait for a lock on a file when using cache-mode full (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-max-depth int                If set limits the recursion depth to this (default -1)
      --vfs-mount-poll-interval duration   Interval to poll the VFS for changes (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-no-check-updatedb            Don't check for updated files in the database
      --vfs-no-modtime                   Don't use modification time as a test in rclone copy/sync
      --vfs-num-complete                 Number of files to complete transfers for when using cache-mode full
      --vfs-read-ahead SizeSuffix        Extra read ahead over --buffer-size when using cache-mode full
      --vfs-read-chunk-size SizeSuffix   Read the source objects in chunks (default 128Mi)
      --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit SizeSuffix If greater than --vfs-read-chunk-size, double the chunk size after each chunk read, until the limit is reached ('off' is unlimited) (default off)
      --vfs-read-chunk-streams int       The number of parallel streams to read at once
      --vfs-read-wait Duration           Time to wait for in-sequence read before seeking (default 20ms)
      --vfs-refresh                      Refreshes the directory cache recursively in the background on start
      --vfs-used-is-size rclone size     Use the rclone size algorithm for Used size
      --vfs-write-back Duration          Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)
      --vfs-write-wait Duration          Time to wait for in-sequence write before giving error (default 1s)

Options shared with other commands are described next. See the global flags page (https://rclone.org/flags/) for global options not listed here.

Filter Options

Flags for filtering directory listings

      --delete-excluded                     Delete files on dest excluded from sync
      --exclude stringArray                 Exclude files matching pattern
      --exclude-from stringArray            Read file exclude patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --exclude-if-present stringArray      Exclude directories if filename is present
      --files-from stringArray              Read list of source-file names from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --files-from-raw stringArray          Read list of source-file names from file without any processing of lines (use - to read from stdin)
  -f, --filter stringArray                  Add a file filtering rule
      --filter-from stringArray             Read file filtering patterns from a file (use - to read from stdin)
      --hash-filter string                  Partition filenames by hash k/n or randomly @/n
      --ignore-case                         Ignore case in filters (case insensitive)
      --include stringArray                 Include files matching pattern
      --include-from stringArray            Read file include patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --max-age Duration                    Only transfer files younger than this in s or suffix ms|s|m|h|d|w|M|y (default off)
      --max-depth int                       If set limits the recursion depth to this (default -1)
      --max-size SizeSuffix                 Only transfer files smaller than this in KiB or suffix B|K|M|G|T|P (default off)
      --metadata-exclude stringArray        Exclude metadatas matching pattern
      --metadata-exclude-from stringArray   Read metadata exclude patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --metadata-filter stringArray         Add a metadata filtering rule
      --metadata-filter-from stringArray    Read metadata filtering patterns from a file (use - to read from stdin)

rclone serve s3server

Serve any remote on the S3 server protocol.

Synopsis

This command implements the S3 server protocol, allowing S3 clients to use rclone as a data storage mechanism for various cloud providers.

To create an S3 server, one must create a Unix or TCP socket that S3 clients will look for when you use the server, and then it listens for commands from the S3 client and runs the corresponding code when necessary. S3 servers can run as a managed server under control of the rclone daemon or as an independent native service. For testing, you can just run it directly from the command line, for example:

sudo rclone serve s3server --socket-addr :8080 -vv

Running rclone serve s3server will create the said socket, listening for commands from S3 clients to create the necessary buckets. Normally you need not give the --socket-addr flag. The API will listen on the unix domain socket at /run/s3server/s3server.sock. In the example above rclone will create a TCP socket and a small file /etc/s3server/s3server.spec containing the socket address. We use sudo because both paths are writeable only by the root user.

If you later decide to change listening socket, the rclone daemon must be restarted to reconnect to /run/s3server/s3server.sock or parse new /etc/s3server/s3server.spec. Until you restart, any bucket related S3 client commands will timeout trying to access the old socket. Running directly is supported on Linux only, not on Windows or MacOS. This is not a problem with managed server mode described in details in the full documentation (https://rclone.org/s3server).

The command will create bucket data under the path given by --data-dir (by default /var/lib/s3server/s3server available only to root) and maintain the JSON formatted file s3server-server.state in the rclone cache directory with book-keeping records of created and mounted buckets.

All mount and VFS options are submitted by the S3 client via API, but you can also provide defaults on the command line as well as set path to the config file and cache directory or adjust logging verbosity.

This command uses the VFS layer. This adapts the cloud storage objects that rclone uses into something which looks much more like a disk filing system.

    --poll-interval duration    Time to wait between polling for changes. Must be smaller than dir-cache-time. Only on supported remotes. Set to 0 to disable (default 1m0s)

However, changes made directly on the cloud storage by the web interface or a different copy of rclone will only be picked up once the directory cache expires if the backend configured does not support polling for changes. If the backend supports polling, changes will be picked up within the polling interval.

You can send a SIGHUP signal to rclone for it to flush all directory caches, regardless of how old they are. Assuming only one rclone instance is running, you can reset the cache like this:

If you configure rclone with a remote control then you can use rclone rc to flush the whole directory cache:

Or individual files or directories:

rclone rc vfs/forget file=path/to/file dir=path/to/dir

The --buffer-size flag determines the amount of memory, that will be used to buffer data in advance.

Each open file will try to keep the specified amount of data in memory at all times. The buffered data is bound to one open file and won't be shared.

This flag is a upper limit for the used memory per open file. The buffer will only use memory for data that is downloaded but not not yet read. If the buffer is empty, only a small amount of memory will be used.

The maximum memory used by rclone for buffering can be up to --buffer-size * open files.

These flags control the VFS file caching options. File caching is necessary to make the VFS layer appear compatible with a normal file system. It can be disabled at the cost of some compatibility.

For example you'll need to enable VFS caching if you want to read and write simultaneously to a file. See below for more details.

Note that the VFS cache is separate from the cache backend and you may find that you need one or the other or both.

    --cache-dir string                     Directory rclone will use for caching.
    --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode             Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
    --vfs-cache-max-age duration           Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
    --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix        Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

•

•

rclone serve (https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve/) - Serve a remote over a protocol.

rclone serve webdav

Serve any remote on the webdav server protocol.

Synopsis

This command implements the WebDAV server protocol, allowing WebDAV clients to use rclone as a data storage mechanism for various cloud providers.

To create a WebDAV server, one must create a Unix or TCP socket that WebDAV clients will look for when you use the server, and then it listens for commands from the WebDAV client and runs the corresponding code when necessary. WebDAV servers can run as a managed server under control of the rclone daemon or as an independent native service. For testing, you can just run it directly from the command line, for example:

sudo rclone serve webdav --socket-addr :8080 -vv

Running rclone serve webdav will create the said socket, listening for commands from WebDAV clients to create the necessary directories. Normally you need not give the --socket-addr flag. The API will listen on the unix domain socket at /run/webdav/webdav.sock. In the example above rclone will create a TCP socket and a small file /etc/webdav/webdav.spec containing the socket address. We use sudo because both paths are writeable only by the root user.

If you later decide to change listening socket, the rclone daemon must be restarted to reconnect to /run/webdav/webdav.sock or parse new /etc/webdav/webdav.spec. Until you restart, any directory related WebDAV client commands will timeout trying to access the old socket. Running directly is supported on Linux only, not on Windows or MacOS. This is not a problem with managed server mode described in details in the full documentation (https://rclone.org/webdav).

The command will create directory data under the path given by --data-dir (by default /var/lib/webdav/webdav available only to root) and maintain the JSON formatted file webdav-server.state in the rclone cache directory with book-keeping records of created and mounted directories.

All mount and VFS options are submitted by the WebDAV client via API, but you can also provide defaults on the command line as well as set path to the config file and cache directory or adjust logging verbosity.

VFS - Virtual File System

This command uses the VFS layer. This adapts the cloud storage objects that rclone uses into something which looks much more like a disk filing system.

Cloud storage objects have lots of properties which aren't like disk files - you can't extend them or write to the middle of them, so the VFS layer has to deal with that. Because there is no one right way of doing this there are various options explained below.

The VFS layer also implements a directory cache - this caches info about files and directories (but not the data) in memory.

VFS Directory Cache

Using the --dir-cache-time flag, you can control how long a directory should be considered up to date and not refreshed from the backend. Changes made through the VFS will appear immediately or invalidate the cache.

    --dir-cache-time duration   Time to cache directory entries for (default 5m0s)
    --poll-interval duration    Time to wait between polling for changes. Must be smaller than dir-cache-time. Only on supported remotes. Set to 0 to disable (default 1m0s)

However, changes made directly on the cloud storage by the web interface or a different copy of rclone will only be picked up once the directory cache expires if the backend configured does not support polling for changes. If the backend supports polling, changes will be picked up within the polling interval.

You can send a SIGHUP signal to rclone for it to flush all directory caches, regardless of how old they are. Assuming only one rclone instance is running, you can reset the cache like this:

kill -SIGHUP $(pidof rclone)

If you configure rclone with a remote control then you can use rclone rc to flush the whole directory cache:

rclone rc vfs/forget

Or individual files or directories:

rclone rc vfs/forget file=path/to/file dir=path/to/dir

VFS File Buffering

The --buffer-size flag determines the amount of memory, that will be used to buffer data in advance.

Each open file will try to keep the specified amount of data in memory at all times. The buffered data is bound to one open file and won't be shared.

This flag is a upper limit for the used memory per open file. The buffer will only use memory for data that is downloaded but not not yet read. If the buffer is empty, only a small amount of memory will be used.

The maximum memory used by rclone for buffering can be up to --buffer-size * open files.

VFS File Caching

These flags control the VFS file caching options. File caching is necessary to make the VFS layer appear compatible with a normal file system. It can be disabled at the cost of some compatibility.

For example you'll need to enable VFS caching if you want to read and write simultaneously to a file. See below for more details.

Note that the VFS cache is separate from the cache backend and you may find that you need one or the other or both.

    --cache-dir string                     Directory rclone will use for caching.
    --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode             Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
    --vfs-cache-max-age duration           Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
    --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix        Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

Supported cache modes are:

•
off: No caching is done. All operations are done directly on the remote. This is the default mode.
•
minimal: Only cache files for reading. Write operations will be done directly on the remote. This mode is useful if you want to read files quickly without writing them. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that read files.
•
writes: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that write a lot of small files or that write frequently to files. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that write files.
•
full: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that need to read and write files frequently, and that require high performance. This mode has the highest compatibility with applications that read and write files.

VFS Options

These flags control the VFS layer behavior. They are used to tune the performance and compatibility of the VFS layer.

      --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode       Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
      --vfs-cache-max-age duration     Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
      --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix  Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
      --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
      --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-disk-cache-recursive        If set, rclone will traverse directories recursively to find files for the disk cache
      --vfs-fast-fingerprint bool       If set, rclone will use a fast fingerprint for checking if files are already in the cache (default true)
      --vfs-fingerprint-method FingerprintHashMethod  Hash method to use for fingerprinting files for the cache (default --vfs-fast-fingerprint)
      --vfs-flag FileFlags               Set flags on VFS objects
      --vfs-flag-exclude stringArray     Exclude VFS objects from flags
      --vfs-flag-exclude-from stringArray  Read VFS flag exclude patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --vfs-flag-include stringArray     Include VFS objects in flags
      --vfs-flag-include-from stringArray  Read VFS flag include patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --vfs-get-content bool             Get the content of files when listing directories (default true)
      --vfs-get-pmod bool                Get the permissions of files when listing directories (default true)
      --vfs-implicit-dirs bool           Create implicit directories when writing files (default true)
      --vfs-lazy-get-pmod                Lazily get the permissions of files when listing directories
      --vfs-lazy-read                  If set, rclone will not read the content of files until they are opened
      --vfs-lock-timeout duration        Time to wait for a lock on a file when using cache-mode full (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-max-depth int                If set limits the recursion depth to this (default -1)
      --vfs-mount-poll-interval duration   Interval to poll the VFS for changes (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-no-check-updatedb            Don't check for updated files in the database
      --vfs-no-modtime                   Don't use modification time as a test in rclone copy/sync
      --vfs-num-complete                 Number of files to complete transfers for when using cache-mode full
      --vfs-read-ahead SizeSuffix        Extra read ahead over --buffer-size when using cache-mode full
      --vfs-read-chunk-size SizeSuffix   Read the source objects in chunks (default 128Mi)
      --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit SizeSuffix If greater than --vfs-read-chunk-size, double the chunk size after each chunk read, until the limit is reached ('off' is unlimited) (default off)
      --vfs-read-chunk-streams int       The number of parallel streams to read at once
      --vfs-read-wait Duration           Time to wait for in-sequence read before seeking (default 20ms)
      --vfs-refresh                      Refreshes the directory cache recursively in the background on start
      --vfs-used-is-size rclone size     Use the rclone size algorithm for Used size
      --vfs-write-back Duration          Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)
      --vfs-write-wait Duration          Time to wait for in-sequence write before giving error (default 1s)

    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

Supported cache modes are:

•
off: No caching is done. All operations are done directly on the remote. This is the default mode.
•
minimal: Only cache files for reading. Write operations will be done directly on the remote. This mode is useful if you want to read files quickly without writing them. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that read files.
•
writes: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that write a lot of small files or that write frequently to files. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that write files.
•
full: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that need to read and write files frequently, and that require high performance. This mode has the highest compatibility with applications that read and write files.

rclone serve (https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve/) - Serve a remote over a protocol.

rclone serve http

Serve any remote on the http server protocol.

Synopsis

This command implements the HTTP server protocol, allowing HTTP clients to use rclone as a data storage mechanism for various cloud providers.

To create an HTTP server, one must create a Unix or TCP socket that HTTP clients will look for when you use the server, and then it listens for commands from the HTTP client and runs the corresponding code when necessary. HTTP servers can run as a managed server under control of the rclone daemon or as an independent native service. For testing, you can just run it directly from the command line, for example:

sudo rclone serve http --socket-addr :8080 -vv

Running rclone serve http will create the said socket, listening for commands from HTTP clients to create the necessary directories. Normally you need not give the --socket-addr flag. The API will listen on the unix domain socket at /run/http/http.sock. In the example above rclone will create a TCP socket and a small file /etc/http/http.spec containing the socket address. We use sudo because both paths are writeable only by the root user.

If you later decide to change listening socket, the rclone daemon must be restarted to reconnect to /run/http/http.sock or parse new /etc/http/http.spec. Until you restart, any directory related HTTP client commands will timeout trying to access the old socket. Running directly is supported on Linux only, not on Windows or MacOS. This is not a problem with managed server mode described in details in the full documentation (https://rclone.org/http).

The command will create directory data under the path given by --data-dir (by default /var/lib/http/http available only to root) and maintain the JSON formatted file http-server.state in the rclone cache directory with book-keeping records of created and mounted directories.

All mount and VFS options are submitted by the HTTP client via API, but you can also provide defaults on the command line as well as set path to the config file and cache directory or adjust logging verbosity.

VFS - Virtual File System

This command uses the VFS layer. This adapts the cloud storage objects that rclone uses into something which looks much more like a disk filing system.

Cloud storage objects have lots of properties which aren't like disk files - you can't extend them or write to the middle of them, so the VFS layer has to deal with that. Because there is no one right way of doing this there are various options explained below.

The VFS layer also implements a directory cache - this caches info about files and directories (but not the data) in memory.

VFS Directory Cache

Using the --dir-cache-time flag, you can control how long a directory should be considered up to date and not refreshed from the backend. Changes made through the VFS will appear immediately or invalidate the cache.

    --dir-cache-time duration   Time to cache directory entries for (default 5m0s)
    --poll-interval duration    Time to wait between polling for changes. Must be smaller than dir-cache-time. Only on supported remotes. Set to 0 to disable (default 1m0s)

However, changes made directly on the cloud storage by the web interface or a different copy of rclone will only be picked up once the directory cache expires if the backend configured does not support polling for changes. If the backend supports polling, changes will be picked up within the polling interval.

You can send a SIGHUP signal to rclone for it to flush all directory caches, regardless of how old they are. Assuming only one rclone instance is running, you can reset the cache like this:

kill -SIGHUP $(pidof rclone)

If you configure rclone with a remote control then you can use rclone rc to flush the whole directory cache:

rclone rc vfs/forget

Or individual files or directories:

rclone rc vfs/forget file=path/to/file dir=path/to/dir

VFS File Buffering

The --buffer-size flag determines the amount of memory, that will be used to buffer data in advance.

Each open file will try to keep the specified amount of data in memory at all times. The buffered data is bound to one open file and won't be shared.

This flag is a upper limit for the used memory per open file. The buffer will only use memory for data that is downloaded but not not yet read. If the buffer is empty, only a small amount of memory will be used.

The maximum memory used by rclone for buffering can be up to --buffer-size * open files.

VFS File Caching

These flags control the VFS file caching options. File caching is necessary to make the VFS layer appear compatible with a normal file system. It can be disabled at the cost of some compatibility.

For example you'll need to enable VFS caching if you want to read and write simultaneously to a file. See below for more details.

Note that the VFS cache is separate from the cache backend and you may find that you need one or the other or both.

    --cache-dir string                     Directory rclone will use for caching.
    --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode             Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
    --vfs-cache-max-age duration           Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
    --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix        Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

Supported cache modes are:

•
off: No caching is done. All operations are done directly on the remote. This is the default mode.
•
minimal: Only cache files for reading. Write operations will be done directly on the remote. This mode is useful if you want to read files quickly without writing them. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that read files.
•
writes: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that write a lot of small files or that write frequently to files. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that write files.
•
full: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that need to read and write files frequently, and that require high performance. This mode has the highest compatibility with applications that read and write files.

rclone serve (https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve/) - Serve a remote over a protocol.

rclone serve gitdav

Serve any remote on the gitdav server protocol.

Synopsis

This command implements the Git-DAV server protocol, allowing Git clients to use rclone as a data storage mechanism for various cloud providers.

To create a Git-DAV server, one must create a Unix or TCP socket that Git clients will look for when you use the server, and then it listens for commands from the Git client and runs the corresponding code when necessary. Git-DAV servers can run as a managed server under control of the rclone daemon or as an independent native service. For testing, you can just run it directly from the command line, for example:

sudo rclone serve gitdav --socket-addr :8080 -vv

Running rclone serve gitdav will create the said socket, listening for commands from Git clients to create the necessary directories. Normally you need not give the --socket-addr flag. The API will listen on the unix domain socket at /run/gitdav/gitdav.sock. In the example above rclone will create a TCP socket and a small file /etc/gitdav/gitdav.spec containing the socket address. We use sudo because both paths are writeable only by the root user.

If you later decide to change listening socket, the rclone daemon must be restarted to reconnect to /run/gitdav/gitdav.sock or parse new /etc/gitdav/gitdav.spec. Until you restart, any directory related Git client commands will timeout trying to access the old socket. Running directly is supported on Linux only, not on Windows or MacOS. This is not a problem with managed server mode described in details in the full documentation (https://rclone.org/gitdav).

The command will create directory data under the path given by --data-dir (by default /var/lib/gitdav/gitdav available only to root) and maintain the JSON formatted file gitdav-server.state in the rclone cache directory with book-keeping records of created and mounted directories.

All mount and VFS options are submitted by the Git client via API, but you can also provide defaults on the command line as well as set path to the config file and cache directory or adjust logging verbosity.

VFS - Virtual File System

This command uses the VFS layer. This adapts the cloud storage objects that rclone uses into something which looks much more like a disk filing system.

Cloud storage objects have lots of properties which aren't like disk files - you can't extend them or write to the middle of them, so the VFS layer has to deal with that. Because there is no one right way of doing this there are various options explained below.

The VFS layer also implements a directory cache - this caches info about files and directories (but not the data) in memory.

VFS Directory Cache

Using the --dir-cache-time flag, you can control how long a directory should be considered up to date and not refreshed from the backend. Changes made through the VFS will appear immediately or invalidate the cache.

    --dir-cache-time duration   Time to cache directory entries for (default 5m0s)
    --poll-interval duration    Time to wait between polling for changes. Must be smaller than dir-cache-time. Only on supported remotes. Set to 0 to disable (default 1m0s)

However, changes made directly on the cloud storage by the web interface or a different copy of rclone will only be picked up once the directory cache expires if the backend configured does not support polling for changes. If the backend supports polling, changes will be picked up within the polling interval.

You can send a SIGHUP signal to rclone for it to flush all directory caches, regardless of how old they are. Assuming only one rclone instance is running, you can reset the cache like this:

kill -SIGHUP $(pidof rclone)

If you configure rclone with a remote control then you can use rclone rc to flush the whole directory cache:

rclone rc vfs/forget

Or individual files or directories:

rclone rc vfs/forget file=path/to/file dir=path/to/dir

VFS File Buffering

The --buffer-size flag determines the amount of memory, that will be used to buffer data in advance.

Each open file will try to keep the specified amount of data in memory at all times. The buffered data is bound to one open file and won't be shared.

This flag is a upper limit for the used memory per open file. The buffer will only use memory for data that is downloaded but not not yet read. If the buffer is empty, only a small amount of memory will be used.

The maximum memory used by rclone for buffering can be up to --buffer-size * open files.

VFS File Caching

These flags control the VFS file caching options. File caching is necessary to make the VFS layer appear compatible with a normal file system. It can be disabled at the cost of some compatibility.

For example you'll need to enable VFS caching if you want to read and write simultaneously to a file. See below for more details.

Note that the VFS cache is separate from the cache backend and you may find that you need one or the other or both.

    --cache-dir string                     Directory rclone will use for caching.
    --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode             Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
    --vfs-cache-max-age duration           Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
    --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix        Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

Supported cache modes are:

•
off: No caching is done. All operations are done directly on the remote. This is the default mode.
•
minimal: Only cache files for reading. Write operations will be done directly on the remote. This mode is useful if you want to read files quickly without writing them. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that read files.
•
writes: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that write a lot of small files or that write frequently to files. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that write files.
•
full: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that need to read and write files frequently, and that require high performance. This mode has the highest compatibility with applications that read and write files.

      --vfs-fast-fingerprint bool       If set, rclone will use a fast fingerprint for checking if files are already in the cache (default true)
      --vfs-fingerprint-method FingerprintHashMethod  Hash method to use for fingerprinting files for the cache (default --vfs-fast-fingerprint)

      --vfs-flag-exclude stringArray     Exclude VFS objects from flags

Cloud storage objects have lots of properties which aren't like disk files - you can't extend them or write to the middle of them, so the VFS layer has to deal with that. Because there is no one right way of doing this there are various options explained below.

The VFS layer also implements a directory cache - this caches info about files and directories (but not the data) in memory.

VFS Directory Cache

Using the --dir-cache-time flag, you can control how long a directory should be considered up to date and not refreshed from the backend. Changes made through the VFS will appear immediately or invalidate the cache.

    --dir-cache-time duration   Time to cache directory entries for (default 5m0s)
    --poll-interval duration    Time to wait between polling for changes. Must be smaller than dir-cache-time. Only on supported remotes. Set to 0 to disable (default 1m0s)

However, changes made directly on the cloud storage by the web interface or a different copy of rclone will only be picked up once the directory cache expires if the backend configured does not support polling for changes. If the backend supports polling, changes will be picked up within the polling interval.

You can send a SIGHUP signal to rclone for it to flush all directory caches, regardless of how old they are. Assuming only one rclone instance is running, you can reset the cache like this:

kill -SIGHUP $(pidof rclone)

If you configure rclone with a remote control then you can use rclone rc to flush the whole directory cache:

rclone rc vfs/forget

Or individual files or directories:

rclone rc vfs/forget file=path/to/file dir=path/to/dir

VFS File Buffering

The --buffer-size flag determines the amount of memory, that will be used to buffer data in advance.

Each open file will try to keep the specified amount of data in memory at all times. The buffered data is bound to one open file and won't be shared.

This flag is a upper limit for the used memory per open file. The buffer will only use memory for data that is downloaded but not not yet read. If the buffer is empty, only a small amount of memory will be used.

The maximum memory used by rclone for buffering can be up to --buffer-size * open files.

VFS File Caching

These flags control the VFS file caching options. File caching is necessary to make the VFS layer appear compatible with a normal file system. It can be disabled at the cost of some compatibility.

For example you'll need to enable VFS caching if you want to read and write simultaneously to a file. See below for more details.

Note that the VFS cache is separate from the cache backend and you may find that you need one or the other or both.

    --cache-dir string                     Directory rclone will use for caching.
    --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode             Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
    --vfs-cache-max-age duration           Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
    --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix        Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
    --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration     Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
    --vfs-write-back duration              Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)

If run with -vv rclone will print the location of the file cache. The files are stored in the user cache file area which is OS dependent but can be controlled with --cache-dir or setting the appropriate environment variable.

The cache has 4 different modes selected by --vfs-cache-mode. The higher the cache mode the more compatible rclone becomes at the cost of using disk space.

Note that files are written back to the remote only when they are closed and if they haven't been accessed for --vfs-write-back seconds. If rclone is quit or dies with files that haven't been uploaded, these will be uploaded next time rclone is run with the same flags.

Supported cache modes are:

•
off: No caching is done. All operations are done directly on the remote. This is the default mode.
•
minimal: Only cache files for reading. Write operations will be done directly on the remote. This mode is useful if you want to read files quickly without writing them. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that read files.
•
writes: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that write a lot of small files or that write frequently to files. This mode has a higher compatibility with applications that write files.
•
full: Cache files for reading and writing. Write operations are written to the cache and then written back to the remote when the file is closed. Read operations are also served from the cache. This mode is useful for applications that need to read and write files frequently, and that require high performance. This mode has the highest compatibility with applications that read and write files.

VFS Options

These flags control the VFS layer behavior. They are used to tune the performance and compatibility of the VFS layer.

      --buffer-size SizeSuffix         Chunk size to buffer file data in RAM (default 16Mi)
      --vfs-cache-mode CacheMode       Cache mode off|minimal|writes|full (default off)
      --vfs-cache-max-age duration     Max time since last access of objects in the cache (default 1h0m0s)
      --vfs-cache-max-size SizeSuffix  Max total size of objects in the cache (default off)
      --vfs-cache-min-free-space SizeSuffix  Target minimum free space on the disk containing the cache (default off)
      --vfs-cache-poll-interval duration Interval to poll the cache for stale objects (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-disk-cache-recursive        If set, rclone will traverse directories recursively to find files for the disk cache
      --vfs-fast-fingerprint bool       If set, rclone will use a fast fingerprint for checking if files are already in the cache (default true)
      --vfs-fingerprint-method FingerprintHashMethod  Hash method to use for fingerprinting files for the cache (default --vfs-fast-fingerprint)
      --vfs-flag FileFlags               Set flags on VFS objects
      --vfs-flag-exclude stringArray     Exclude VFS objects from flags
      --vfs-flag-exclude-from stringArray  Read VFS flag exclude patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --vfs-flag-include stringArray     Include VFS objects in flags
      --vfs-flag-include-from stringArray  Read VFS flag include patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --vfs-get-content bool             Get the content of files when listing directories (default true)
      --vfs-get-pmod bool                Get the permissions of files when listing directories (default true)
      --vfs-implicit-dirs bool           Create implicit directories when writing files (default true)
      --vfs-lazy-get-pmod                Lazily get the permissions of files when listing directories
      --vfs-lazy-read                  If set, rclone will not read the content of files until they are opened
      --vfs-lock-timeout duration        Time to wait for a lock on a file when using cache-mode full (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-max-depth int                If set limits the recursion depth to this (default -1)
      --vfs-mount-poll-interval duration   Interval to poll the VFS for changes (default 1m0s)
      --vfs-no-check-updatedb            Don't check for updated files in the database
      --vfs-no-modtime                   Don't use modification time as a test in rclone copy/sync
      --vfs-num-complete                 Number of files to complete transfers for when using cache-mode full
      --vfs-read-ahead SizeSuffix        Extra read ahead over --buffer-size when using cache-mode full
      --vfs-read-chunk-size SizeSuffix   Read the source objects in chunks (default 128Mi)
      --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit SizeSuffix If greater than --vfs-read-chunk-size, double the chunk size after each chunk read, until the limit is reached ('off' is unlimited) (default off)
      --vfs-read-chunk-streams int       The number of parallel streams to read at once
      --vfs-read-wait Duration           Time to wait for in-sequence read before seeking (default 20ms)
      --vfs-refresh                      Refreshes the directory cache recursively in the background on start
      --vfs-used-is-size rclone size     Use the rclone size algorithm for Used size
      --vfs-write-back Duration          Time to writeback files after last use when using cache (default 5s)
      --vfs-write-wait Duration          Time to wait for in-sequence write before giving error (default 1s)

rclone serve (https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_serve/) - Serve a remote over a protocol.

rclone serve redisdav

Serve any remote on the redisdav server protocol.

Synopsis

This command implements the Redis-DAV server protocol, allowing Redis-DAV clients to use rclone as a data storage mechanism for various cloud providers.

To create a Redis-DAV server, one must create a Unix or TCP socket that Redis-DAV clients will look for when you use the server, and then it listens for commands from the Redis-DAV client and runs the corresponding code when necessary. Redis-DAV servers can run as a managed server under control of the rclone daemon or as an independent native service. For testing, you can just run it directly from the command line, for example:

sudo rclone serve redisdav --socket-addr :8080 -vv

Running rclone serve redisdav will create the said socket, listening for commands from Redis-DAV clients to create the necessary directories. Normally you need not give the --socket-addr flag. The API will listen on the unix domain socket at /run/redisdav/redisdav.sock. In the example above rclone will create a TCP socket and a small file /etc/redisdav/redisdav.spec containing the socket address. We use sudo because both paths are writeable only by the root user.

If you later decide to change listening socket, the rclone daemon must be restarted to reconnect to /run/redisdav/redisdav.sock or parse new /etc/redisdav/redisdav.spec. Until you restart, any directory related Redis-DAV client commands will timeout trying to access the old socket. Running directly is supported on Linux only, not on Windows or MacOS. This is not a problem with managed server mode described in details in the full documentation (https://rclone.org/redisdav).

The command will create directory data under the path given by --data-dir (by default /var/lib/redisdav/redisdav available only to root) and maintain the JSON formatted file redisdav-server.state in the rclone cache directory with book-keeping records of created and mounted directories.

All mount and VFS options are submitted by the Redis-DAV client via API, but you can also provide defaults on the command line as well as set path to the config file and cache directory or adjust logging verbosity.
